\section[(my own line)]{Your own line — the first writing with no model}

\label{lesson:PT-W256-my-own-line}



\begin{quote}
Everything you have written in Portuguese so far had something to reach for — a shape to trace, a word to copy, a sound to take down.

This does not. You choose the words, from a supply that is closed: only what this book has taught you.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Write \textbf{one line} about yourself: your name, where you live, and a language you speak. The verbs are ones you already hold — \textbf{chamo-me}, \textbf{moro}, \textbf{falo} — and the \emph{-o} already says \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}, so no \textbf{eu} is needed.

One thing to decide on purpose before you start: \textbf{the marks are letters, not decoration.}

The marks over a Portuguese vowel do two different jobs. The accent in \textbf{português} marks the vowel that carries the stress. The \textbf{til} in \textbf{pão} and \textbf{irmã} is not an accent at all: it marks a \textbf{nasal} vowel, a sound rather than a stress.

A hand that writes \textbf{pao} for \textbf{pão} has not written Portuguese untidily. It has written a word Portuguese does not have, and left the reader to guess.

Write the line. Then read it back and check every mark \textbf{before} you check anything else.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Is the til on \textbf{pão} an accent? (\textbf{No} — it marks a nasal vowel, not the stress.)

And what did you choose here that the earlier writing lessons chose for you? (\textbf{The words.})
\end{tcolorbox}
